title: On the Diophantine Equation $p^x+ (2p+1)^y =z^2$ with Consecutive Exponents
summary: We determine all positive integer solutions to $p^x+(2p+1)^y=z^2$, where $p$ is an odd prime and $|x-y|=1$. The unique solution is $(x,y,z)=(2,1,p+1)$ except when $p=7$, for which there is one additional solution, $(x,y,z)=(4,3,76)$. The proof reduces the nontrivial factorization case to an auxiliary equation, bounds its exponents using an AM--GM inequality, and isolates the exceptional solution with a divisibility argument modulo $2k^2$.
